memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: At that time Abimelek and Phicol the commander of his forces said to Abraham, "God is with you in everything you do. Now swear to me here before God that you will not deal falsely with me or my children or my descendants..." - Gen 21:22-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abimelech - the same king Abraham had once deceived - comes to him and says something remarkable: "God is with you in everything you do." A pagan king can see the hand of God on Abraham's life. Despite Abraham's failures, the evidence of God's blessing and presence was so clear that even an outsider recognised it. Abraham's life pointed beyond himself to God.

This is worth pausing over. Abraham was far from perfect - he had lied to this very king. And yet, over time, the reality of God's presence in his life became undeniable, even to unbelievers. God's faithfulness shone through despite Abraham's flaws. Our witness does not depend on being flawless, but on God being visibly with us.

There is a challenge here. Can others look at our lives and sense that God is with us? Not because we are perfect, but because there is something about the way we live, the way we handle blessing and hardship, that points to a God at work. Our lives are meant to be evidence that draws others to notice God.

Jesus said, "Let your light shine before others, that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven" (Matt 5:16). The goal is not that people admire us, but that they see God in us. May it be said of us, as of Abraham, that "God is with you in everything you do" - a reputation that speaks not of our greatness, but of His presence.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Can others sense that God is with you, even through your imperfections?
- Does your life point beyond yourself to God at work?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, let my life be evidence that You are with me, not because I am perfect, but because You are faithful. May others see You at work in me and be drawn to glorify You. Shine through my imperfections.
Amen.
